# 4 Maccabees Chapter 11 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** The Mother's Speech and Deaths

---

**1** The most admirable mother embraced each of her sons in turn as they were brought out, and spoke to them in their ancestral language: My son, have pity on me — I carried you in my womb for nine months and nursed you for three years.

**2** I urge you, my child, to look at the sky and the earth and everything in them, and know that God made all of it out of nothing.

**3** And so it is that he who made all things also made you — and if you turn your heart toward him and receive his comfort, you will live.

**4** I am not afraid of this tyrant. I will willingly share in your sufferings, in the hope of shaming this brutal tyrant.

**5** I am your father, your mother, your nurse, your guide, and your teacher of wisdom. I urge you: do not be afraid, for you did not come into this world without the will of God.

**6** Think on all this and do not lose heart, for it is for the sake of the law that you are dying.

**7** She was still saying these things as the guards led her away to her death.

**8** O most wretched of all tyrants! Most barbarous of all! Does your heart not break when you see how they look at you?

**9** Does pity not grip you when you see this aged mother of seven being treated this way?

**10** And yet she bears it all with joy for the love of God.

**11** She is truly a mother of virtue — for it is God who plants virtue in the soul.

**12** Now indeed, O tyrant, you have unjustly put these seven brothers to death.

**13** But you have not enslaved their reason, and you have not conquered their virtue.

**14** It is you who have been conquered — by reason! You who hold power over entire nations have been defeated by an old woman and her seven sons.

**15** The noble mother of the seven, having watched all seven of her sons die, and having encouraged them all to a noble death, ended her own life in the same noble way.

**16** She maintained her spirit as if she were going to a great celebration, glorying in God — nothing could break her.

**17** Let this story be sufficient proof that devotion mastered by reason can overcome even the worst suffering.

**18** For if a woman, and she an aged woman, together with her seven sons could overcome a tyrant, it is clear that devotion to God is master of the passions.

**19** I have shown this through the wise men I named, and also through the story of the seven brothers and their mother.

**20** All of them together have proved the sovereignty of reason over the passions.

**21** It is fitting that I call them blessed — Eleazar and the seven brothers and their mother.

**22** Having endured all their sufferings and torments and burnings, they have been victorious. The holy ones now reign; they are at rest with their ancestor Abraham. Not one of them failed or wavered.

**23** Not one of the brothers said, I wish I had never come to this! Not one of them said, I wish I had eaten the forbidden food!

**24** Not one of them turned back; not one shrank from death; not one was robbed of the reward of courage. From the first to the last, every one of them held firm.
